title: Stacks, Heaps, Trees & Backtracking
description: Drawn from practiced problems: Remove K Digits, Minimize Deviation in Array, Maximum Depth of Binary Tree, Subsets.

questions.prompt: Remove K Digits (smallest number after removing k digits) is built on which data structure?
questions.explanation: Greedily pop while the stack top is greater than the current digit (and k remains) to keep the result monotonically non-decreasing.

questions.prompt: Minimize Deviation in Array repeatedly adjusts the current extreme. Which structure gives the needed extreme in O(log n)?
questions.explanation: Normalize odds up by *2, then keep evens in a max-heap, halving the max while tracking the running min to minimize the spread.

questions.prompt: Maximum Depth of a Binary Tree via DFS returns 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)).
questions.explanation: Each node contributes 1 plus the deeper of its two subtrees; an empty node contributes 0.

questions.prompt: What general technique enumerates all Subsets by including/excluding each element with undo steps?
questions.explanation: Backtracking: choose to include or skip each index, recurse, then undo the choice.

questions.prompt: Implement subsets(nums): return all 2^n subsets of a list of distinct integers, in any order.
questions.explanation: Backtracking emits the current partial set at every node of the decision tree. Graded manually against the exemplar (no code runner).
